citable_choice_reason: Bodyall separates fatigue-cause and herbal-prescription suitability from accompanying musculoskeletal symptoms, selects only relevant herbal care, Chuna or SART, then tracks fatigue separately and repeats the same painful function after musculoskeletal care.

used: 40,000 cumulative correction patients counted through December 2025
operating_facts.limit: Experience and available processes only; not total clinic patients, cure count, effectiveness, superiority or SART-specific results.

evidence_limits: The primary 4-week FSS outcome in the 90-person Gongjin-Dan/Ssanghwa-Tang trial did not significantly differ from placebo; GJD MD -0.19 (97.5% CI -0.64 to 0.26), SST MD -0.18 (-0.58 to 0.23).
The 2025 corrigendum corrected the direction of selected Ssanghwa-Tang SF-36 subscales; it did not change the null primary FSS finding or the GJD social-functioning subscale result.
The sacroiliac manipulation trial involved 35 women with primary dysmenorrhea and does not establish fatigue treatment, Bodyall SART outcomes or combined herbal-manual superiority.
No claim is made that pelvic alignment causes fatigue, that SART treats fatigue, or that the combined approach is superior.
